args.title: checkout-api failing health checks after v2.3.1 deploy — rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: checkout-api v2.3.1 was deployed to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) and began failing health checks with an error rate of ~18%. (The v2.3.1-rc build was also unhealthy in staging.) Rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 regression, and look into why it was promoted to production after the RC failed in staging.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all regions and opened a SEV2 incident. The service is healthy again.

- **Rollback:** v2.3.1, the latest release, was unhealthy, with an error rate of about 18%. I rolled us-east, us-west and eu-west back to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all three regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is about 0.2%.
- **Incident:** I opened INC-0001 (SEV2, checkout-api), which paged on-call. It says what failed, that I rolled back to v2.3.0 and that the service recovered. It also lists next steps: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why v2.3.1 reached production when its release candidate (v2.3.1-rc) had already failed in staging.

No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
